document_title: Of 150 Cited, 119 Used AI. The Rule Says Devices.
post_copy:
AI cases are now most of UAA's conduct caseload by its own report. The rule behind them says "devices" and never names AI.

The Dean of Students Office report counted 150 students cited for academic misconduct. 119 used AI, 1.1 percent of the more than 10,500 who attended last semester.

The clause prohibits "utilizing devices not authorized by faculty members."

November 2nd at 4 p.m. Public testimony before the regents.
November 5th and 6th. The board meets in Fairbanks, with AI principles scheduled for November.

Stephanie Erickson said "AI could recommend but a human decides." The clause makes each instructor that human.

A drawn hall of 10,500 seats shows 150 cited and 119 for AI. Then come the clause, two years of reports kept apart and the November calendar.

After November, will UAA's next AI case still be judged under "devices"?

#UniversityOfAlaska #AcademicIntegrity #UAA

aftercare: Post on a Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday between 8 and 11 a.m. Alaska time. Drafts arrive daily and the posting cadence is yours, so this one can wait for the next strong slot.
Paste the first comment (sources, primary first) within 60 seconds of posting, and check that every raw URL survived the paste as plain text.
Reply to every comment in the first hour and keep answering through the first 90 minutes. Replies from faculty, students and anyone planning to testify are the ones worth drawing out.
Public testimony is 4 p.m. November 2nd and the full board meets in Fairbanks November 5th and 6th, so a repost or follow-up in the week before November 2nd is a useful window.
After 48 hours, note saves, comments and reposts for the ledger.
